summary.text: The kinetic theory of gases is a simple classical model that treats a gas as numerous tiny particles in constant, random motion.
It uses the particles' collisions with each other and with the container walls to explain how volume, pressure and temperature relate, as well as viscosity, thermal conductivity and diffusion.
Daniel Bernoulli laid its basis in 1738, arguing that particle impacts on a surface cause pressure and that average kinetic energy sets temperature.

facts.label: Basic model
facts.value: Describes an ideal gas with perfectly elastic collisions

facts.label: Bernoulli's work
facts.value: Hydrodynamica, 1738, laid the basis of the theory

facts.label: Maxwell distribution
facts.value: Formulated in 1859, the first statistical law in physics

facts.label: Brownian motion papers
facts.value: Einstein and Smoluchowski made accurate predictions from the theory

facts.label: Ancient idea
facts.value: Lucretius proposed bodies were made of rapidly moving atoms

items.prompt: Why does gas push outward on the inside of a sealed tank?

options.label: The particles slowly leak through the metal
The particles press down because of their weight alone
Countless moving particles strike its surface
The particles stick to the surface and pull on it

items.explain: Bernoulli argued that the impact of molecules on a surface causes the pressure of the gas.

items.prompt: Two sealed tanks hold the same gas, one hotter than the other. What differs between them?

options.label: The hotter gas has bigger molecules
The hotter gas has greater average kinetic energy per molecule
The cooler gas has more collisions with perfect elasticity
The cooler gas has molecules at rest

items.explain: The average kinetic energy of the molecules determines the temperature of the gas.

items.prompt: In the basic model, how does the size of gas particles compare with the typical distance between them?

options.label: They are about the same as the distance apart
They are larger, so they constantly touch
They vary so no comparison can be made
They are much smaller than the distance apart

items.explain: The model assumes the particles are much smaller than their average distance apart.

items.prompt: Why was Bernoulli's theory slow to be accepted?

options.label: Energy conservation was unproven, so elastic collisions seemed unclear
Nobody believed gases could exert pressure
It predicted that gases could not be heated
It treated particles as larger than their container

items.explain: Conservation of energy had not yet been established, and it was not obvious how collisions could be perfectly elastic.

items.prompt: A warm metal spoon looks perfectly still. What is true of its particles?

options.label: They are still, since nothing visible moves
They are moving, but too tiny for us to see
They move only when the spoon is touched
They are large, but hidden by the spoon's shape

items.explain: Motion remains hidden in warm bodies because of the extremely small sizes of the moving particles.

items.prompt: Gas molecules do not all travel at the same speed. What did Maxwell's distribution describe?

options.label: The distance a molecule travels before hitting another
The number of walls in a container
The share of molecules moving at speeds in a given range
The single speed every molecule reaches in time

items.explain: Maxwell's distribution gave the proportion of molecules having a certain velocity in a specific range.
